title: Budget enforcement and cost governance
subtitle: Spend is a first-class control in my substrate: a fail-closed daily budget on GPU provisioning that agents cannot raise from inside the provisioning path, per-second accounting, and cost attributed to the work order that spent it.

lede: I build spend control into the path that spends, and I keep its key in human hands. Rented capacity and metered APIs get hard gates; model usage inside governed work gets attribution. Agents on FAFO Core and Function Forge can stand up GPU capacity, and a rented GPU bills from power-on whether anyone remembers it or not. I decided the spending limit would live inside the provisioning path, and that its only key would be a person at a terminal. The limit is a daily dollar cap on the operator's calendar. A day runs from local midnight to local midnight in a timezone stored once, so every host computes the same day.
quote: I kept projections out of the check because an exact rule is easier to trust.
evidence: Cost governance for cloud GPUs: a fail-closed daily cap checked before any port, container or cloud call, set only by a person at a terminal, and a cap of $0 on any day without a budget.

Real-time spend accounting: per-second cost to a hundredth of a cent from the provider's confirmation, updated every 10 s in Redis, recomputed under a lock in Lua, paid containers stopped by a 30 s pass.
API budget enforcement: units reserved before each call against a monthly budget and reconciled with the vendor's usage figures, warning at 80 percent and refusing at 100.
Cost attribution for AI work: model usage split into token classes, priced against a public model-price catalog and attributed to the work order, role, persona, runtime and model that spent it.
author: Corey James
